back: Farming without synthetic fertilisers or pesticides, using manure, compost, rotation, legumes and biological control.
Growing plants without soil, roots in a nutrient solution or an inert medium fed with solution.
A crop whose DNA has been changed by genetic engineering, often with a gene from another species.

front: What does the Bt gene make a crop produce?
back: A protein (from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis) that kills certain caterpillars, e.g. stem borers and bollworms.
Higher yields, less insecticide, better nutrition, possible drought or disease tolerance.
Pest and weed resistance, gene flow, costly patented seed, non-target effects, market rejection.

front: Arguments for and against organic production
back: For: no residues, healthier soil, premium prices. Against: lower yields, more labour, harder pest control, certification costs.
High cost, technical skill, dependence on electricity, rapid spread of water-borne disease.
Hydroponic system in which a thin film of nutrient solution flows past roots in sloping channels and is recirculated.
